title: Two distinct molecular cloud populations detected in massive galaxies
question: What are the bulk motions, physical properties, and locations of molecular clouds seen via intrinsic absorption against compact radio continuum sources in massive galaxies?

recipe.goal: Continuum subtraction and spectral cube imaging
recipe.method: Subtract continuum and image measurement sets using uvcontsub and tclean at the narrowest channel width with natural and uniform weighting
key_parameters: deconvolver = hogbom; weighting = natural or uniform; narrowest possible channel width

recipe.goal: Generate moment maps and extract spectra against the radio core
recipe.method: Create moment 0, 1, and 2 maps using immoments and extract spectra at the position of the compact radio continuum source
key_parameters: includepix = [0,100] for moment 0 maps with overlapping absorption; >4 sigma threshold for moments 1 and 2 maps

recipe.goal: Fit Gaussian components to emission and absorption spectra
recipe.method: Incrementally add Gaussian lines and fit with SciPy curve_fit, masking absorption while fitting overlapping emission first, then run 10,000 Monte Carlo simulations for uncertainties
key_parameters: Stopping criterion: no channel > 5 sigma and fitting region RMS < 1.5 times remainder RMS; 10,000 Monte Carlo realizations
assumptions: Errors from fitting emission do not significantly propagate to overlapping absorption fits

recipe.goal: Calculate excitation temperatures and absorption column densities
recipe.method: Compute excitation temperatures from CO(2-1)/CO(1-0) velocity-integrated optical depth ratios (Eq. 2) and column densities using optical-depth corrected LTE formula (Eqs. 3 and 4)
key_parameters: T_ex = 5 K for column density calculations
assumptions: Local thermodynamic equilibrium, ground state excitation temperature T_ex = 5 K, optical depth correction factor tau / (1 - exp(-tau))

recipe.goal: Estimate molecular gas masses and disk inclinations from CO emission
recipe.method: Calculate molecular gas mass from CO emission integral using Bolatto et al. (2013) relation (Eq. 5) and estimate disk inclination from axis ratios
assumptions: Standard Milky Way CO-to-H2 conversion factor and circular disk with r_0^2 = 0.2

score_reason: All 13 ALMA project codes, observing dates, integration times, CASA version (6.6.3.22), imaging tasks, and analytical equations (with key conversion factors and cosmology) are explicitly stated, and best-fit line parameters are released as supplementary material; however, custom scripts, exact tclean/uvcontsub parameters, extraction apertures, and visual masking windows are not provided.
rediscovery_reason: All ALMA data are public in the archive, the data reduction and Gaussian fitting procedures use standard CASA and SciPy tools, and the main results (molecular gas masses, optical depth ratios, excitation temperatures, and absorption column densities) are quantitative and tabulated.
